audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1] through phases[4] said 'Skill' while win[1] through win[4] said 'Anivia' — four rows of the level chart rendering two different answers on the same page.
audit.why: The packet levelChart gives Anivia rows 0-4, and the content whys for those rows all describe Anivia dictating the lane. The content layer is the one that matches the data.
audit.corrected: phases[1..4].side flipped to 'Anivia' as one atomic group, matching win[1..4], which already held the correct value. Rows 5 and 6 already agreed on 'Aurelion Sol'.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3], whys[6] and late credited a 'global ultimate', a 'global Comet' and a '5-star Comet'.
audit.why: Aurelion Sol has no global ability; his R is 1250 range. Comet is a rune, not a spell, and 'stars' are stardust stacks.
audit.corrected: Late spike rekeyed to stacked stardust and The Skies Descend at 1250 range.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions were absent: Flash Frost's stun cancels Breath of Light and Astral Flight (both interruptible channels), and Crystallize does NOT trap Aurelion Sol because Astral Flight flies over terrain.
audit.why: ownerKit Q and W both carry channel: 'interruptible — any CC cancels it'; brief.missingInteractions rule 'your-channel-punished'. ownerKit W text: 'Aurelion Sol flies over terrain in a targeted direction.' Anivia W is a terrain wall at 17s. Frostbite also only doubles off Flash Frost or a fully formed Glacial Storm, so one dodge blanks the rotation.
audit.corrected: spikes[0], early, breakdown.cooldowns and enemyWin now state the channel cancel; mid states the wall is a wasted answer against a banked Astral Flight; breakdown.carry states the Frostbite doubling condition.

audit.why: Flash Frost is 11s at rank 1, Astral Flight 22s, Frostbite only 4s but conditional.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with the real clocks and the doubling condition.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.carry, dosFull[1].d, dontsFull[2].d and enemyWin were name-swappable templates.
audit.why: Every one of them would read the same with any other enemy substituted.
audit.corrected: Grounded in Flash Frost's range and channel cancel, Frostbite's doubling condition, and the black hole out-clearing under a wall.

edits.before: Anivia wins by landing Flash Frost (Stun), denying your pattern, and out-ranging your plan one polite trade at a time.
edits.after: Anivia wins by landing Flash Frost to cancel your channel, doubling Frostbite on the chilled target, and walling off the retreat.

edits.before: - Anivia Flash Frost (Stun): matchup-defining — The slow-moving stun starts every Anivia kill — sidestep it and her E never doubles. It governs your forward steps. - W Astral Flight spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Anivia Flash Frost: 11s at rank 1 — the slow-moving stun starts every kill, cancels your channel, and doubles her Frostbite; sidestep it and none of that happens. - Astral Flight, 22s: crossing her wall, not poking. - Hold R for a fight that decides something.

edits.before: Carry by scaling honestly — every stardust stack is permanent, and the 30-minute version of you wins fights your laning self cannot imagine.
edits.after: Carry by farming through her: Frostbite is 4s and cheap, but it only doubles off Flash Frost, so dodging one spell blanks her whole rotation.

edits.before: W-flyby: fly a lateral arc, drag Q across Anivia for two seconds of burn + stacks, and land outside his answer range — repeat forever from one item.
edits.after: The black hole out-clears her caster minions from 750 while Crystallize is up, and every execute tick banks stardust she has no way to contest.

edits.before: Channelling Q face-to-face inside his engage range with W down — every champion that touches you wins that exchange pre-items.
edits.after: Flash Frost stuns down its whole line from 1075 — flying into a loaded one cancels the flight mid-air, inside her Glacial Storm.

edits.before: Two-item global presence and ultimate burst outscale her zone-control kit in full fights
edits.after: Two items of stardust scaling and black-hole zoning outscale her zone-control kit in fights

edits.before: Flash Frost and Frostbite chip you from safety while Crystallize walls off your escape or engage routes, controlling the entire lane.
edits.after: Flash Frost stuns at 1075 range and doubles her Frostbite, and it cancels your beam channel outright — Crystallize does the zoning after.

edits.before: Your global Comet and 5-star ultimate outscale her zone-control kit once she can't wall off an entire team fight.
edits.after: Stacked stardust and The Skies Descend outscale her zone control once she cannot wall off an entire teamfight.

edits.before: Anivia's Flash Frost-into-Frostbite combo chips huge chunks of your HP from a range your early Q arc can't threaten back, and Crystallize can wall you away from minions or cut off your escape entirely. Rebirth means even a good trade doesn't kill her, so you're fighting an uphill battle on both damage and kill potential. Farm passively under tower pressure, dodge Flash Frost by holding off-angle, and don't commit stars into a lane you can't punish yet.
edits.after: Anivia's Flash Frost-into-Frostbite combo chips huge chunks of your HP from 1075 range, where your 750 beam cannot answer, and the stun cancels your channel the instant it lands. Rebirth means even a good trade doesn't kill her, so you are fighting uphill on damage and on kill potential. Farm passively under tower pressure, hold an off-angle so Flash Frost has to be aimed rather than fired down the lane, and don't commit stars into a lane you can't punish yet.

edits.before: She continues to control space with wall placement and long-range poke, and her egg form means your all-in math always has to double — kill her body, then kill the egg before it hatches. You're still on the back foot here, unable to force fights she doesn't want, so prioritize denying her freeze-and-poke setups with wave management instead. Any all-in attempt before your first item is likely to trade unfavorably even with jungler help.
edits.after: Crystallize cannot cage you: Astral Flight crosses terrain, so her 17-second wall is a wasted answer whenever you keep the flight banked. Her egg still doubles your all-in math — kill the body, then the egg before it hatches — so you stay on the back foot, denying her freeze-and-poke setups with wave management rather than forcing fights she does not want. Any all-in before your first item trades badly even with jungler help.

edits.before: Once your first core item lands, your Q-W burst finally threatens to kill through both her HP bar and the Rebirth egg in a single combo, flipping the damage race. By two items your global ultimate and 5-star Comet outscale her zone-control kit — she can wall a skirmish but can't wall an entire teamfight from your ultimate's range. Force fights where her wall placement can't isolate your team, and punish her for over-extending Flash Frost.
edits.after: Once Rod of Ages lands, a held beam plus the black hole's execute finally kills through both her HP bar and the Rebirth egg in a single pass, flipping the damage race. By two items The Skies Descend outscales her zone control — she can wall off a skirmish but cannot wall a teamfight out of a 1250-range drag. Force fights where her wall placement cannot isolate your team, and punish an over-extended Flash Frost.

notes: Four chart rows (1-4) disagreed between phases[].side ('Skill') and win[] ('Anivia'). Resolved toward the content layer, which matches both the packet chart and the whys text; proposed as one atomic group. The best previously-unstated fact in this matchup: Astral Flight flies over terrain, so Crystallize cannot wall Aurelion Sol in or out — it is now in breakdown.cooldowns and mid. Glacial Storm's listed cooldown (4/3/2) is the toggle recast, not a fight-to-fight clock, so I did not quote it as a punish window.
